text: FP16 has an 11-bit significand, so it holds every integer exactly only up to 2,048; between 2,048 and 32,768 the spacing of representable values is 2, 4, 8 and then 16, so in Google's E4B file at FP16 a position near 30,000 shares its rounded value, and therefore its rotary phases, with up to 15 neighbouring positions.

text: Because the fastest rotary frequency of both E4B layer types is exactly 1 radian per position (inverse frequency 1.0), rounding a position by d positions shifts the phase of those dimensions by d radians: at FP16 near position 30,000 that is up to 8 radians, more than a full turn.
